characters.name: In General
characters.description: A group of crusty, monster-like creatures indigenous to Grouchland. Bad Is Good and Good Is Bad: This is their culture. Big Ol' Unibrow: As mentioned under Oscar's entry, it's a species trait. Bizarro Universe: Grouch society mirrors human society (right down to similar celebrities — Dan Rather-Not and Donald Grump, for example), but they prefer unhappiness and filth to happiness and cleanliness. Blue-and-Orange Morality: As explained above, they dislike (often downrightcondemn) nice and pleasant things, and like things that most other people would find unpleasant. Although a bit odd, it sounds simple enough, right? Well, this also means that they like feeling miserable, and yet the nice things they hatemakethem miserable, which theylikeand... yeah. Try not to think about it too hard.

characters.name: Alistair Cookie
characters.description: The host ofMonsterpiece Theater. He is basically Cookie Monster in a red robe. Ambiguous Situation: It's unclear whether or not he's just a persona for Cookie Monster or a separate character. His 2025 appearance onJeopardy!—in a video clue under aSesame Streetcategory—implies the former, asJeopardy!hostKen Jenningsintroduced him as Cookie Monster but Cookie himself, in Alistair Cookie robe, introduced himself under the identity. Big Eater: He snacks on cookies offscreen during the entirety of theMonsterpiece Theateropening, with crumbs spilling over the title. Catchphrase: "Good evening, and welcome toMonsterpiece Theater. Me your host, Alistair Cookie." Do Not Adjust Your Set: When he introducesMonsters With Dirty Faces, he tells viewers not to adjust their TV sets, because the movie is in black and white.

characters.name: Cookie Monster
characters.description: The very incarnation of gluttony. He loves cookies more than anything, but has been seen talking about "healthy" food, so kids can make good decisions in regard to nutrition. Cookie Monster has starred in several skits of his own in recent years, most recently "Cookie Monster's Foodie Truck", where he and Gonger (fromThe Furchester Hotel) visit the source of the missing ingredient of a recipe assigned to them by a child (Cookie's insatiable hunger is usually the reason why that ingredient is missing). Me got me ownpagetoo, if you want to hear me read these tropes! Affectionate Nickname: The monster's closest friends, including Prairie Dawn and Gonger, often refer to him as "Cookie". Anti-Role Model: He eats terrible, unhealthy food nonstop, and he's proud of it. However, he does stress the importance of healthy food.Then again, he also eats non-food. The Artifact: His tendencies to eat everything are derived from his earlier appearances before his character was established as Cookie Monster. He was originally just an unnamed monster who devours anything, including non-foods, within reach. The character would soon shape up to be the monster we know and love today, gaining both name and hisTrademark Favorite Food. Nonetheless, his trait to devour inedibles within his reaching path has long endured to this day.

characters.name: Cookie Monster's baby cousin
characters.description: Cookie Monster's cousin, who appeared in a sketch where he's trying to feed her cookies, but she does not want to eat one. Then Ernie appears with some groceries filled with fruits and vegetables (which Cousin Monster would go with). Cookie Monster complains that he loves cookies, but his baby cousin would not touch them. And Ernie explains maybe she does not like cookies, and tells Cookie Monster that he has to feed his baby cousin something else. Big Eater: Has quite a big appetite. Does Not Like Spam: Implied. She doesn't seem interested in cookies. Trademark Favorite Food: She loves fruits (such as an apple), and vegetables (such as carrots and celery). She would never touch cookies at all.

characters.name: Frazzle
characters.description: An orange monster with big teeth. Face of a Thug: Has horns, thick eyebrows, prominent fangs, and yellow schlerae, but is actually friendly. Hulk Speak: In his"I Am" Song, The Frazzletones explain that his signature growl can mean many different things. Picky Eater: Sometimes when eating croissants, he refuses other foods. Trademark Favorite Food: Likes croissants because they remind him of his horns.

characters.name: Grover
characters.description: A well-meaning, multitalented monster who suffers more humiliation and injury than the rest of the cast combined. He also goes as a superhero named Super Grover. (He became Super Grover 2.0 in 2010.) Affectionate Parody:"SU...PER GROVER!" parodies characters from theSuperherogenre, with the absurd outfit and hammy tendencies of many of those characters."Look at yourself. Now back to me. Now back to yourself. Now back to me.Sadly, you are not a monster..."The "Near & Far" sketch gets parodied itself quite a bit.This stintas aDiscoDancing RoyaltyalaSaturday Night Fever.Thesketchesin the restaurant underwentMemetic MutationviaThe Daily Show with Jon Stewart. "SU...PER GROVER!" parodies characters from theSuperherogenre, with the absurd outfit and hammy tendencies of many of those characters. "Look at yourself. Now back to me. Now back to yourself. Now back to me.Sadly, you are not a monster..." The "Near & Far" sketch gets parodied itself quite a bit.

characters.name: Herry
characters.description: A large, blue monster. He's strong and has a gruff voice but he is very sweet. Always wanting to help out but usually inadvertently ended up breaking more than he fixed. Herry was a main character on the show from Season 2 (1970-1971) until Season 31 (2000). Badbutt: Was meant to be the "tough guy" among the cast. Being from a show for preschoolers, you obviously can't gettootough... The Big Guy: He's very big. Blind Without 'Em: Episode 1261 reveals that he's near-sighted, so he is taken to the eye doctor for some glasses. Blue Is Heroic: A blue furred monster who is very nice.

characters.name: Maurice
characters.description: A light blue monster with a large green nose. Mostly used as a background monster, though he is the focus of a few segments. Alliterative Name:MauriceMonster. Chewing the Scenery: At the end of "Beginning, Middle, End", he gets so emotional and over-the-top in his performance that his backup singers have to literally drag him off the stage. A Day in the Limelight: While Maurice is often a background character, he has a few notable roles, such as the song "Beginning, Middle, End", the game show "Say the Word", and a few street scenes. Hidden Depths: Maurice is a surprisingly good trumpet player. He's been a member of the Easy Listening Monster Band and once did backup music for Herry's song "Furry Blue Mommy of Mine".

characters.name: Telly
characters.description: A neurotic, easily discouraged monster. Was best friends with Oscar; now best friends with Baby Bear. He also has an obsession with triangles. Artifact Name: His name, "Telly Monster", originates from his early characterization, where he was obsessed with watching TV.He grew out of that trait over time, but the name stuck anyway. Characterization Marches On:He was originally obsessed with television, but grew out of that over the years.Brian Muehl originally characterized Telly as painfully insecure, perpetually worried, and always needing reassurance from others to build confidence. When Martin Robinson took over the character, he initially stuck to Muehl's portrayal, but overtime, he evolved Telly into a character with a very wide, and very powerful, range of emotions. He was originally obsessed with television, but grew out of that over the years. Brian Muehl originally characterized Telly as painfully insecure, perpetually worried, and always needing reassurance from others to build confidence. When Martin Robinson took over the character, he initially stuck to Muehl's portrayal, but overtime, he evolved Telly into a character with a very wide, and very powerful, range of emotions.

characters.name: Two-Headed Monster
characters.description: Art Imitates Life: The character was created when Jerry Nelson and Richard Hunt were goofing around on the set one day and told everyone they were a two-headed monster. Big Eater: Implied. Both heads share a body (and therefore, a stomach), but eat separate meals. Big Ol' Eyebrows: One of the Two-Headed Monster's heads has them. Verging on aBig Ol' Unibrow. Conflict Ball: A lot of sketches involve the two heads arguing over simple things. The monster's first appearance was Olivia telling a story about how the heads can never agree on what to do, which they eventually solve by taking turns. Drama Queen: More like Drama King. Sometimes, he/they overact/s, for example, when one head cries because the other has more milk.

characters.name: Aristotle
characters.description: A blind, grey monster who enjoys collecting things. Collector of the Strange: Some of the things he's collected are lettuce, broken sports gear, and bologna sandwiches. In-Series Nickname: Ari Non-Standard Character Design: He's one of the only monsters to be built with ears.

characters.name: Deena
characters.description: An energetic, pink monster who has red hair, wild rolling eyes, and a passion for play. She lives in a cave with her caretaker, Pearl. Genki Girl: She takes her energy to extremes rarely met by the otherSesame Streetmonsters, which is unsurprising, as the performer of Deena would later become best known for portraying Red Fraggle onFraggle Rock. Put on a Bus: Writer Norman Stiles says he created Deena, named after one of his friends, to emphasize the role of play in the development of the brain at a time when it was not promoted widely. Stiles would eventually recall that "for whatever reason, as we tried the character in a few sketches, Deena’s insistence on playing was more annoying than amusing". However, Karen Prell believed her own performance of the character,which was deemed "over-the-top" in an interview,led to her short time on the series. Regardless, both Deena and Pearl saw dramatically reduced roles starting in the twelfth season, and one of their last known appearances together was in the wedding sequence ofThe Muppets Take Manhattan. The Deena puppet would eventually morph into the character of Humphrey. Third-Person Person: Before Elmo came along, she had the tendency to refer herself in third person ("DEENA WANTS TO PLAY!").

characters.name: Elmo
characters.description: A 3½-year-old monster who speaks in a high-pitched voice and normally talks in third person. Was best friends with Zoe; now best friends with Abby Cadabby. Hosts theElmo's World,Elmo the Musical, andElmo and Tango's Mysterious Mysteriessegments, as well asThe Not-Too-Late Show with Elmo, and the object of 1996's Tickle-Me-Elmo craze. And Elmo’s gota self demonstrating pagetoo! Adaptation Dye-Job: Some illustrated and animated depictions of Elmo (such asThe Monster at the End of this Storyand theFurry Friends Foreverspecials) change his purple eyelids to dark red. All-Loving Hero: He likes everyone, even Oscar. "Elmo loves you." Ascended Extra: Pretty much the ultimate of this trope. He started out as a utility monster puppet, but shortly after was christened the name Elmo. Brian Muehl and later Richard Hunt performed him in a handful of episodes between 1980-1984, but when Kevin Clash took over, Elmo became a much more prominent character and is now the star of the show.

characters.name: Leo the Party Monster
characters.description: An orange, pink-haired monster who's obsessed with partying, to the extent that he even hosts a talk show on the subject. Companion Cube: He's almost never seen without his portable radio, so he can have his party music on the go with him. Large Ham: He hasNO INDOOR VOICE, and rarely lets a sentence finish without some sort of exhortation to "PAAAAARTAAAYYYYYY!" Large Ham Title: Besides regularly appending his name with "the Party Monster", he also refers to himself as "Leo, The Total Party Monster of the Known Universe" at one point. Life of the Party: Leo views himself as this,especiallyin situations where there's no actual party happening.

characters.name: Natasha
characters.description: A baby monster. Her parents are Humphrey and Ingrid. Baby See, Baby Do:Natasha's first words (oh dear) came from copying Snuffy.Natasha copies the Count when he sings to her in one episode.Inverted once, when Humphrey copies Natasha. Natasha's first words (oh dear) came from copying Snuffy. Natasha copies the Count when he sings to her in one episode. Inverted once, when Humphrey copies Natasha.

characters.name: Pearl
characters.description: A brown monster who lives in a cave with Deena, for whom she serves as a caretaker. She likes peace and quiet, which is often difficult for her to achieve because of Deena's relentless energy. Put on a Bus: Both Deena and Pearl saw dramatically reduced roles starting in the twelfth season, and one of their last known appearances together was in the wedding sequence ofThe Muppets Take Manhattan. The Pearl puppet later became used for extras in various sketches, minus her orange tuft of hair. Team Mom: Often tries to calm down her roommate, especially when that character's overtly energetic tendencies come into play.

characters.name: Ruby
characters.description: A bright red haired orange-yellow monster who loves learning experience and research on everything. Cloud Cuckoo Lander: A lot of her experiments are, odd to say the least. For Science!: Much of what she does, no matter how silly it might be, is all for the purpose of doing an experiment. Reused Character Design: She's basically Leo the Party Monster with different hair and a smaller nose. Security Blanket: In the "Guys and Dolls" song from Monsterpiece Theater, she loves playing with her toy truck.

characters.name: Baby Tooth and the Fuzzy Funk
characters.description: The three Muppet monster dancers who appeared in the 1990s. They sometimes dance with humans. Butt-Monkey: Baby Tooth. Despite being the frontman, sometimes one of the Fuzzy Funk will literally kick him offscreen. Genre Roulette: Their numbers feature all kinds of music genres from hip-hop to classical, from jazz to hoedown, from Caribbean music to traditional Asian dances. The Speechless: They never talk or sing, they just dance.

characters.name: Humphrey and Ingrid
characters.description: Baby Natasha's parents. Humphrey and Ingrid work as employees at the Furry Arms hotel. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: Humphrey wears a red spotted necktie with a white collar. Affectionate Nickname: Ingrid and Humphrey call Natasha many pet names. They even sing a song about it in one episode. Ambiguously Related: There's a monster named Freda played by Ingrid's puppet. Being related might explain the family resemblance. Cloud Cuckoolander: Let's just say that Humphry and Ingrid can be rather... dense. Much to the chagrin of most of the people on Sesame Street.

characters.name: Merry Monster
characters.description: A tiny, squeaky voiced monster. NO INDOOR VOICE: her whole shtick.

characters.name: The Monster Cookie
characters.description: A giant talking cookie who is, to put it simply, a personification of the phrase "You are what you eat". He appeared in a 1992 sketch, where Cookie Monster has a nightmare after devouring the entire box of cookies his grandmother sent him to serve at his birthday party. The Monster Cookie tells Cookie Monster the sad story of how he became a cookie. He used to be a furry monster as well, but hiscookie-only dietcaused him to turn into a cookie, and he regrets that he never ate healthier foods. As Cookie Monster wakes up from his sad dream, he sees one more cookie, but then declares that he will never eat cookies again. He devours some carrots, a fish, and some whole wheat bread. But then, seeing as how the cookie isn't talking or crying, he eats it, remarking, "Well, maybe sometime a cookie!" Anthropomorphic Food: He's a giant cookie. As Cookie Monster is about to eat him, he angrily shouts, "Keep your hands off, pal!" Dream People: He only appeared in a dream, so he's likely not a real monster. One-Shot Character: He appeared only once, in Cookie Monster's dream. Polka-Dot Disease: The first symptom of his becoming a cookie was when he started to "break out in chocolate chips".

characters.name: Rosita
characters.description: A 5-year-old bilingual monster who plays guitar. She was originally patterned after a fruit bat, but lost the wings in Season 35 through 51. She stated in an interview that they just popped off when flying. Blue Is Heroic: While her fur is not as deep of a blue as Grover or Herry's, she's just as kind. Continuity Nod: Luis taught her how to play the guitar, and she has retained that skill very well. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: For the first thirteen years of the character, Rosita had a pair of wings, and we've seen her use them to fly (or rather, attempt to; a couple of 1990s episodes have her discover that she can't actually fly). 2004 onward, the wings disappeared and there has never been an explanation as to why on the show. According to her puppeteer, the choice was made by the merchandising wing ofSesame Street. In 2021, however, Rosita grew back her wings. Emotional Language Shift: She speaks Spanish when happy (although she speaks it a lot when angrytoo).

characters.name: Super Morphin Mega Monsters
characters.description: Superhero versions of Elmo, Zoe, Telly, and Rosita. They are a parody of the showMighty Morphin' Power Rangers. Age Lift: They seem to be somewhat older versions of the four monsters, as they now worry about problems like studying for math tests in their civilian lives. Animal Theme Naming: They have dinosaur-themed names: Elmosaurus, Zoeceratops, Telly Dactyl, and Rosita Raptor. They don't have really anything to do with dinosaurs, though, so it's just aShout-Outto the source material. Badass Pacifist: Unlike the Power Rangers, they would save the day by reasoning with the villains' targets. By the Power of Grayskull!: They transform by shouting "Morphin time!", followed by calling out their individual identities.

characters.name: Zoe
characters.description: A monster who was added in the 1990s in order to add balance to a predominantly male cast. She is good friends with Elmo and Big Bird. She started wearing a tutu regularly in 2002, so people wouldn't be confused on whether she's a boy or a girl, but it was removed in 2017, now wearing it occasionally. Cloudcuckoolander: This is a girl who treats a rock as if it were a living being. Consulting Mister Puppet: Zoe's pet rock, Rocco, who she talks to in spite ofElmo's sarcastic rebukes (insistently reminding her that Rocco is just an inanimate rock). The Cover Changes the Gender: She did a cover of theSesame Streetsong "Fur". Demoted to Extra: Even though Zoe used to be included in almost all marketing and merchandise for the series back in the 90s and early-to-mid 2000s, she has been getting this treatment more and more ever since Abby Cadabby was introduced in 2006, after which Abby pretty much replaced Zoe as Elmo's best friend. Despite this, Zoe still often shows up in new storylines and even had a focus episode in season 50 where she breaks her arm.

characters.name: Louie
characters.description: Elmo's father, who is a loving dad and ambiguously in the military. Good Parents: He, along with Mae, seem to be very supportive parents. Not So Above It All: Normally very level-headed, but he did sing a song about the potty in "Elmo's Potty Time".Truth in Television, some parents do sing to their kids to get them interested in potty training. Unexplained Accent: He, Mae, and his sister in law Jill have Southern accents, though Sesame Street is in New York. Although his late brother Jack had a Brooklyn accent.

characters.name: Mae
characters.description: Good Parents: She seems to be a loving mother.

characters.name: The Monster Clubhouse Monsters
characters.description: Four energetic monsters named Phoebe, Googel, Mel and Narf. They have a club called the Monster Clubhouse, where they do wacky things like get chased by elephants. Aerith and Bob: Phoebe and Mel are common names. Googel and Narf, not so much. Breaking the Fourth Wall: They often talk to the viewers. Cloud Cuckoo Lander: They have strange interests like being chased by elephants. Demoted to Extra: After Season 34, the Monster Clubhouse segments were discontinued since kids were not too familiar with the characters, resulting in the monsters becoming background characters.

characters.name: Murray
characters.description: A fluffy orange monster with a round, oversized jaw who rose to fame by hosting a variety of recurring segments; namelyWord on the StreetandMurray Has a Little Lamb. These are unique in that they're kept separate from the regularSesame Streetscenes by being set in the "real world" where Murray has largelyunscripted scenesinteracting with "normal" people, with his Spanish-speaking lamb Ovejita. Alliterative Name: His surname is implied to be "Monster". Amusing Injuries: Frequently. Usually in the form ofThe Pratfall. The Cameo: Murray very rarely appears in "street scenes". Joey Mazzarino has said that he prefers for Murray to be kept in the "real world" à laUncle Traveling Matt. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Has proven to be his fate following Mazzarino's departure from the series in 2015, due to the show's format and runtime change that came with its move of first-run episodes from PBS to HBO.Matt Vogelconfirmed in a May 2016 Facebook post that there were no plans to recast Murray because "it's such a Joey character".His regular "Tune-in" segments were dropped entirely (barring a few reused "Murray Has a Little Lamb" segments)and his only new appearances in that season were for a few celebrity musical numbers. Despite this, he remained in the show's opening and closing sequences until 2021. In 2022, however, the Murray puppet began appearing as a generic monster onAhlan Simsim, an Arabic co-production ofSesame Street.

characters.name: The Furchesters
characters.description: Elmo's uncle Fergus, aunt Funella, and cousin Phoebe, who runThe Furchester Hotelin the United Kingdom. Alliterative Family: Downplayed. Fergus and Funella have names beginning with F, but Phoebe's, though it sounds the same, begins with P-H. Alliterative Name: Their names begin with F or P-H and their surname is Furchester (Funella), Fuzz (Fergus) and Furchester-Fuzz (Phoebe). Breaking the Fourth Wall: They sing to the audience at the end of all their skits. Catchphrase: "Fuzzawubba!" for Phoebe, whenever she gets an idea.

characters.name: Gonger
characters.description: A marble-mouthed monster chef who first appeared onThe Furchester Hotel(the British co-production) before joining the domestic show for the "Cookie Monster's Foodie Truck" segments. Due to his weird voice, he very often mispronounces certain words: "pinea-pap-ple", "cran-ba-berry", "cheeeeeeese" "bana-na-na-na-na", etc, as well as adding an "h" sound to words that begin with a vowel. Angry Chef: He often gets angry at Cookie Monster for eating the last ingredient from their recipe. Ascended Extra: His first appearances onFurchesterwere simply banging a gong to signal Monster Tea Time (hence his name). By the second season, he gained a much more prominent role as the hotel chef. From there, he became the co-star to the new Cookie Monster segment, "Cookie Monster's Foodie Truck". Within a couple of short years, he now has merchandise and walk-around versions in parks and live shows. Boke and Tsukkomi Routine: Gonger spends a lot of time correcting Cookie Monster's misconceptions on the food they're making. Catchphrase: *bangs a gong* "IT'S READY!"

characters.name: Rudy
characters.description: A blue-haired orange monster who is Abby Cadabby's stepbrother, introduced in Season 47 to help introduce kids to blended families. He has a habit of "borrowing" his stepsister's wand without her permission. Hilarity Ensues: Whenever he gets his hands on Abby's wand. Interspecies Romance: Rudy's dad, a monster, married Abby's mom, a fairy, which explains how he and Abby became stepsiblings in the first place. Welcome Episode: "Hello Rudy"

characters.name: Karli
characters.description: A young monster who was initially in foster care before moving back with her mother and was written to teach kids about foster care and parental addiction. While we don't know much about her as a person (apart from the fact that she has some toy elephants, plays soccer, and likes PB&J and pizza), she has a complex story line: she used to live alone with her mother, but then her mother got addicted to an unknown substance. While the mother was in rehab, Karli was fostered by a couple named Clem and Dalia. Now, Karli is living with her mother again, but the mother is still in group therapy. Alliterative List: Has a list of "Seven 'C's" to do with her mother's addiction: she didn'tcause it, she can'tcontrol it, she can'tcure it, but she can help takecare of herself,communicate her feelings, make healthychoices, andcelebrate herself. Ambiguously Absent Parent: No sign of her dad. Companion Cube: Has a stuffed elephant named Elephant. Foster Kid: She was introduced living with a foster family.

characters.name: The Amazing Mumford
characters.description: A Large Lavender Live Hands Anything Muppet bumblingStage Magicianwhose magic never works quite right. Beach Episode: "Imagine That" had a subplot of him trying to go to the beach. Big Ol' Eyebrows: To the extent that they cover his eyes completely. Catchphrase: He says, "A la peanut butter sandwiches" when he makes a spell. Exact Words: When Grover asks him to make a carrot disappear, Mumford gladly obliges - by eating it.Mumford: Magic? Who said anything about magic?

characters.name: Betty Lou
characters.description: A Hot Pink Anything Muppet little girl who likes dolls and is four years old. Advertised Extra: Despite being a minor character in the show, she appeared in a lot of books in the 70s and 80s. Ascended Extra: She would appear a lot more in the books than the show, often as one of the main characters. Then in the 1990s, she appeared more in the show too. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: She disappeared after Season 29. She made her last overall appearance in the 2009 book "What's Different?". Early-Installment Weirdness: In the first season sketch "Pick Your Pet", the character went under the name of Lucy Jones.

characters.name: Biff and Sully
characters.description: A pair of construction workers who work together. Dreadful Musician: Biff. He's a good singer, but multiple episodes show that he can't play the piano very well, unlike Sully. Expy: Biff is based on the overly-talkative taxi cab passenger that Jack Burns played in his recurring comedy sketches with Avery Schreiber (who played the driver).noteBurns had quite a few Muppet connections, including being the head writer of the first season ofThe Muppet Showand co-writingThe Muppet Movie. Eyes Always Shut: Sully's eyebrows are very visible, but his eyes aren't. Handy Man: They're construction workers who are always building or fixing something.

characters.name: Count von Count
characters.description: An Ambiguously Undead Large Lavender Live Hand Anything Muppet guy with fangs, a Romanian accent, and a love of counting. He lives in a castle with a number of bats and has been seen dating various Countesses. And here’s one!One linkto my self demonstrating page! Ah-ah-ah! Ambiguously Jewish: His songs are frequently based on klezmer. He also has the stereotypical large nose. However, he celebrates Christmas. Badass Cape: Wears a long, flowing vampire's cape. Although it’s a bit unusual: it’s dark green with a triangular collar, and the inside has a colorful confetti-like pattern. In episodes where a green screen is required, his cape is purple. Bad "Bad Acting": Ina Vanity Fair video where various Sesame Street characters do impressions of each other, his are consistently the worst: he always keeps his own accent, and usually seems at a loss for what to say. His impression of Ernie almost comes off as a roast:Count-as-Ernie:I am here to annoy you!

characters.name: Forgetful Jones
characters.description: A Large Lavender Live Hands Anything Muppet cowboy with poor memory. Accidental Misnaming: Because of his forgetfulness, he often calls people by the wrong names. Not Clementine and Buster, though, which shows just how dear they are to his heart. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: He always forgets what he's supposed to do, but once he's been reminded, he seems to be pretty good at his job as a cowboy. Catchphrase: Says, "Awwwwww. I forget!" a lot. Cowboy: He lives and works on a ranch raising cattle, rides a horse, and is almost never seen without his cowboy hat and western duds. However, he once found it difficult to remember just what he did for a living, leading to Clementine and others doing a musical number to try and remind him. It didn't work, and a despairing Clementine declared that there was nothing to do but give up. Forgetful retorted, "Us cowboys never give up!"

characters.name: Guy Smiley
characters.description: Ambiguously Jewish: Guy Smiley is just aStage Name; his real name is Bernie Liederkrantz, as he stated in one "Beat the Time" sketch. Demoted to Extra: Was mostly retired for years after Jim Henson's death, to the point ofThe Character Died with Him. He did appear in the two PC games,Let's Make A Word!andGet Set to Learn!in the mid 90's and his puppet form has recently been brought back with new material. Game Show Host: In most of his appearances, he has played this role. Large Ham: Often hams things up. NO INDOOR VOICE: To the point where Jim Henson hated doing the character; it was hard on his throat. In order to do multiple takesandavoid putting strains on his throat, he usually pre-recorded the lines that would be spoken by the character in his sketches.

characters.name: Mr. Johnson
characters.description: A grumpy old customer of Charlie's restaurant where his waiter is Grover. Ascended Extra: Granted, he's been on the show since the early years, but he's gained a bit more prominence in later years, appearing in more street stories, and sometimes without Grover. Berserk Button:Neversuggest he has beady eyes. Big Eater: Subverted. His overweight appearance and the fact that he is constantly at restaurants would suggest this, but in one sketch, he couldn't eat two slices of pizza. Butt-Monkey: In nearly every appearance he makes, something unlucky happens to him.Mr. Johnson:[referring to Grover]Everywhere I go, I see that guy! I'm starting to think I'm under some sort of spell!

characters.name: Prairie Dawn
characters.description: A Hot Pink Anything Muppet, pageant-obsessed girl who aspires to a career in journalism. Catchphrase: "Oh, dear!" is her catchphrase, usually followed by a groan. Demoted to Extra: Although she was featured in much of the merchandise (books, records, toys, etc.), Prairie was not on the show much during the first two decades. Through the 1990s to the late 2000s, she started to be seen on a much more regular basis. Shortly after, she nearly vanished until just before Fran Brill retired. Prairie started to appear somewhat regularly afterwards, except for seasons 50 and 51. Deadpan Snarker: Becomes one in the game showThe Triangle Is Rightdue to it being "a dumb game". Drama Queen: Rants whenever she's upset or frustrated.

characters.name: Sherlock Hemlock
characters.description: A Green Anything Muppet somewhat inept detective. Like many others, he's fallen by the wayside over the past decade or so. Captain Ersatz: It goes without saying that he wearsa deerstalker cap and tweed Inverness cape. Catchphrase: He often shouts, "Egad!" and "Gadzooks!". Clueless Detective: He has a tendency to miss the obvious when solving "mysteries". The Ditz: Sometimes forgets that he did some of the "crimes" himself.

characters.name: A to G
characters.description: Age-Appropriate Angst: His launching into full-on blues mode because his blankie is being washed is typical of a baby. Brainy Baby: Is able to speak in full sentences despite being a baby. No Celebrities Were Harmed: Obviously based on earlyRock & RolllegendFats Domino. Something Blues: One of his songs is called "Baby Blankie Blues". They are the fabulous insect four who sang "Letter B", "Thinking of U", and "Hey Food" (with Cookie Monster). They appear as both Lavender and Green Anything Muppet insects.

characters.name: H to M
characters.description: Butt-Monkey: He thinks the hotel has bad service, but actually, he's just the unluckiest guest. Annoying Laugh: An obnoxious high-pitched chuckle that was eventually too much for Frank Oz's vocals. Brought to You by the Letter "S": He often invokes this trope by putting letters on people's clothes. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Besides the fact that voicing him was too hard on Frank Oz, the other main reason for his being dropped was that he was only good for that one joke. Despite this, his segments continued to appear in new episodes until 2001. Since then, Harvey has made two return appearances—first in a sketch in 2010 and then in the 50th Anniversary special in 2019. A Day in the Limelight: He got an entire season 7 street segment, where he sang a"Tell a Joke", to the annoyance of Susan, Luis and Bob.

characters.name: N to R
characters.description: A scientist who often either thinks he's invented or discovered something only to find out it's already been invented/discovered or uses mundane objects for crazy reasons. Blatant Lies: In one skit, he claims not to be unhappy while sobbing (and by the context, it clearly isn'tTears of Joy). Buffy Speak: He tended to give his inventions (of things that had already been invented) names in this style, like "carry-keeper" (lunchbox), "story-carry" (book) and "dirt-pusher" (broom). Cloud Cuckoo Lander: Among other things, he thought socks weren't invented yet and thought using a balloon to "find the sky" was something most people were inclined to do. Ditzy Genius: He's talented enough to be an award-winning scientist, yet he often goofs up due to lacking basic facts.

characters.name: S to Z
characters.description: A Fat Blue Anything Muppet who has an unusual way of talking. He would replace some words with sound effects. Alliterative Name: His first and last names begin with "S". Meaningful Name: He can speak in sound effects and his last name is Soundman. Stock Sound Effects: He has the ability to speak with added sound effects. For example: In one of the Grover the Waiter sketches, Simon said to Grover, "I would like to buy a[clucks like a chicken]sandwich!" In another sketch, he wanted to use Ernie's telephone, but Ernie had trouble understanding him. Unsatisfiable Customer: When he was at Charlie's, Simon ranted, "Why did my brother recommend this restaurant? The service is terrible." It may be that Simon Soundman's brother is the usual customer, Mr. Johnson. And both are Fat Blue Anything Muppets originally performed by Jerry Nelson. Although, if this is true, it would seem that their brotherly relationship may be rocky...

characters.name: Alex
characters.description: An Orange Muppet kid who has a father in prison. He was introduced in 2012 as part ofSesame Street'sLittle Children: Big Challengeson the subject of Incarcerated parents as they help children nationwide with parents or other relatives who are in jail or prison. Prison Episode: His father violated the law (an adult rule), and had to go to prison. Other characters taught Alex about incarceration.

characters.name: Bert
characters.description: Long-suffering roommate andBlue Oni to Ernie's Red Oni. Bert would generally prefer to be left alone with a book than put up with his friend's shenanigans. He also really likes pigeons and oatmeal. Aside Glance: Similar toOliver Hardy, he'll often do one of these in exasperation. Berserk Button: Donotlose his bottle caps or paper clips. Bookworm: Likes to read, and likes to have quiet when he reads. But that’s quite a challenge when you’re dealing with Ernie. The Bore: According to Oz, he originally considered Bert a very boring character... then made his dullness his definitive character trait. His hobbies andtaste in foodare all what most people would consider typically "boring" things.

characters.name: Bruno
characters.description: A Garbage man who carries Oscar the Grouch's trashcan. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He was retired when the foam interior of the puppet ended up disintegrating after years of storage, and it would have been too expensive to rebuild. Suddenly Voiced: Although Bruno is usually a silent character, he did speak a few times (like in the end ofFollow that Bird, He replied to Oscar "Sure, Boss!"). He even sang with The Trashmen with the song, "Put it in the trashcan".

characters.name: Ernie
characters.description: An enthusiastic, extroverted prankster who's Bert's roommate andRed to Bert's Blue.He enjoys taking baths with his rubber duckie. Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other: The thought of being seperated from Bert and never seeing him again is enough to drive him to tears. Baths Are Fun: He loves taking baths, which was established in the very firstSesame Streetepisode (when he did the "I call my bathtub Rosie" joke), and reiterated with numerous bathtub sketches and songs (including theBreakaway Pop Hit"Rubber Duckie"). Cloud Cuckoo Lander: Frequently does weird things like talking to a rubber duck or waking up the whole neighborhood with loud off-key opera just so he can know what time it is at night. These are usually harmless yet annoying, but on rare occasions, Ernie's antics reach borderline dangerous levels. Case in point, in a sketch where Bert is teaching Ernie a pattern game, Ernie plays using farm animals instead of paperclips and bottlecaps. Bert telling Ernie to not use farm animals again when playing another round results in Ernie unleashing an elephant into the apartment, and the pachyderm almost immediately starts wrecking the place as Bert, Ernie and the farm animals run for their lives. Consulting Mister Puppet: Ernie often talks to his trademark rubber duckie about his problems.

characters.name: Ji-Young
characters.description: A Korean-American Muppet who plays electric guitar and loves skateboarding. First introduced in 2021. Tomboy: Ji-Young's interests include playing electric guitar and skateboarding. She also wears generally masculine clothing and has aTomboyish Ponytail.

characters.name: Julia & her family
characters.description: A little girl who has autism, an alternate neurology which some folk consider a disorder. Introduced in 2017 in the wake of increased diagnoses (1 in 68 children) of autism and autism-spectrum disorder conditions. Big Brother Worship: She always cheers for her big brother Samuel at his soccer games and loves to play with him. Breakout Character: Introduced as the world's first autistic Muppet, she has become an instant hit with audiences and is in almost as much merchandise as the other characters. Broken Record: Has a bit of echolalia when talking with other characters, but also repeats some of what she, herself, says. Catchphrase: "Play, play, play!"

characters.name: Felix the Grouch
characters.description: An old friend of Oscar's. Oscar worries that he isn't a real Grouch anymore since he's become a neat freak, but it turns out he's still grouchy. My Species Doth Protest Too Much: In contrast to the other Grouches, he prefers to be clean. He even tries to vacuum Oscar's trash can. Odd Couple: With Oscar, directly referencing the play the trope is based on. Shout-Out: ToThe Odd Couple, which stars a messy character named Oscar and a neat-freak character named Felix.

characters.name: Mrs. Grouch
characters.description: Oscar's mother, and also the mother of his sister Bunny and brother Ernest. Doting Parent: Loves her children in a weird grouchy way.

characters.name: Grundgetta
characters.description: Affectionate Nickname: Oscar calls her "Grungy". All Women Love Shoes: As a grouch, her taste in shoes is, well, different than most women, but she does enjoy shoe-shopping with Maria, and she's known to squee over a pair she likes. Hair-Trigger Temper: She gets angry easily due to being a Grouch. Meaningful Name: Her name comes from the term "grunge", which is a type of grime or dirt. Morality Pet: One of few street residents Oscar is rarely grouchy with.

characters.name: Irvine
characters.description: Baby Talk: Can't speak in full sentences yet. Bratty Half-Pint: Is just as cranky as her uncle. Commander Contrarian: As not only a very young child but also aGrouchchild, Irvine stubbornly refuses to do anything she's told to do, unless they know how to use Grouch logic to handle her. This is best shown in episode 2529 where she's being babysat by Maria, who simply can't get Irvine to eat her food. Up until Oscar takes pity on Maria and reveals she just needed to tell Irvinenoteat that food, whereupon Irvine starts wolfing down her meal with an eagerness befitting Cookie Monster. Sick Episode: Gets the "grouch flu" in one episode. Vague Age: Described as a baby but can say quite a few words and walk quite well, however, she's clearly very young.

characters.name: Oscar the Grouch
characters.description: An irritable, antisocial Grouch who lives in aBigger on the Insidetrash can with his worm, Slimey, and his elephant Fluffy. You’d better not come to myself demonstrating page! I like my alone time! Adaptational Heroism: Oscar takes up this role inThe Adventures of Elmo in Grouchlandwhen he volunteers to go with Zoe, Telly, Gordon, Big Bird, Maria, and Cookie Monster to venture to Grouchland and get Elmo's stolen blanket back from Huxley. Affectionate Nickname: He is called "Oskie" by Grundgetta. Anti-Role Model: One purpose of the character is to poke fun at irritable people.

characters.name: Alice Snuffleupagus
characters.description: Snuffy's two-year-old sister. Annoying Younger Sibling: Downplayed. Sometimes gets in Snuffy's way, but isn't a complete brat. Baby Talk: Has trouble speaking correctly due to her young age. Character Tics: Stares at the wall when sad. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Lasted over a decade on the show and hasn't been mentioned since she was removed, although she continued to be seen on the show's float in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade for a few years afterwards.

characters.name: Baby Bear
characters.description: The smallest of the Three Bears. (Later, the second-smallest of the Four Bears.) He is best friends with Telly Monster. Alliterative Name:BabyBear. Annoying Younger Sibling: Although he has a great relationship with Curly, and is usually patient with her, she annoys him every now and then. Bread, Eggs, Breaded Eggs: "He's a hero, he's a guy... Hero Guy!" Early Installment Character-Design Difference: From Seasons 22 to 29, as well as various other productions up toElmopalooza, Baby Bear had duller fur, eyes closer together, and an overall much chunkier figure.

characters.name: Benny
characters.description: A grumpy rabbit who serves as the bellhop for the Furry Arms hotel. Berserk Button: Doesn't like being called "bunny" or being touched. Half-Dressed Cartoon Animal: Wears a coat but no pants. Hates Being Touched: He doesn't like people touching him. He even wrote a song called "Don't Touch Me". Heel–Face Revolving Door: In the series' 25th anniversary special, "Sesame Street All-Star 25th Birthday: Stars and Street Forever!", Benny was the only citizen of Sesame Street who supported Ronald Grump's plan to turn the neighborhood into the Grump Tower, as he wanted to work as the tower's doorman. However, when Grump revealed that he was planning to build a robotic doorman for the project, Benny quickly joined the rest of Sesame Street to stop Grump's plan.

characters.name: Big Bird
characters.description: An inexplicably large, yellow bird, perpetually stuck at age 6. Mr. Snuffleupagus is his best friend. He lives in a nest near the apartments. International adaptations of the show feature alternate equivalents of the character, who areapparently Big Bird's cousins, including Pino fromSesamstraatand Abelardo fromPlaza Sésamo. Affectionate Nickname:Snuffy calls him "Bird".Luis often calls him "Pájaro".His aunt Nani Bird calls him "Manu Nui". Snuffy calls him "Bird". Luis often calls him "Pájaro".

characters.name: Chip and Dip
characters.description: Two cat brothers who like to pull pranks on Oscar. They look identical, but you can tell them apart because one of them has a deeper voice. Cats Are Mean: Downplayed. They're not mean, just pranksters. The Prankster: They enjoy playing pranks on Oscar. Self-Deprecation: They self-identify as "mangy". Theme Twin Naming: Implied. Their namesrhyme, and their song reveals that they're brothers and started talking around the same time, hinting that they're twins or at least came from the same litter.

characters.name: Curly Bear
characters.description: Baby Bear's toddler sister. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: Wears a diaper and a pink bow. Annoying Younger Sibling: Downplayed. While she sometimes annoys Baby Bear, she doesn't do it all the time and they generally get along fine. Baby See, Baby Do: When Baby Bear mentions that his parents are going out to dinner, she shouts, "Dinner!". Baby Talk: Can't speak 100% properly yet.

characters.name: Davey and Joey Monkey
characters.description: A pair of monkeys that appeared on Sesame Street in the '80's and '90s. Catchphrase: Well, They love "BANANAS!" Put on a Bus: The two stopped appearing on the show after Season 29.They eventually returnedin Episode 5023 (part of Season 50), where they tossed their banana peels on the ground, causing Zoe to slip on them and break her arm. Those Two Guys: They're always seen together. Trademark Favorite Food: "BANANAS!"

characters.name: Gladys the Cow
characters.description: One of the various Muppet cattle inhabiting Sesame Street. The Diva: Has a very high opinion of herself, and tends to hog the spotlight (asMumford can tell you), but she means well. Eat the Camera: She does so in the Waiter Grover "Coffee Plant" skit, going berserk and chasing Mr. Johnson after drinking the cup of coffee Grover just made for him. Apparently she doesn't handle caffeine well. "I Am" Song: "I'm Proud to be a Cow". Species Subversives: Gladys and Miss Moody break the stereotype of cows being common farm beasts and speak in posh accents.

characters.name: Granny Bird
characters.description: Big Bird's grandmother. Cool Old Lady: A kindly old bird. Costume Evolution: Around the time of Season 46, Granny Bird's glasses are now larger with black frames, and has swapped her pink shawl with a mint green silk scarf. Non-Mammalian Hair: Book illustrations depict her with a full head of white hair, despite not having such on the show. Not Allowed to Grow Old: Despite being a senior, Granny Bird shows no signs of aging between the time Big Bird becomes the perma-six-year-old of today.

characters.name: Hoots the Owl
characters.description: An old bluesman and sax player. Comically Missing the Point: He tells Cookie Monster that cookies are a sometimes food... but doesn't care about Cookie Monster eating stuff that'snot food. Destined Bystander: He (or, at least, the puppet that would later come to be him) first appeared in a single scene inSesame Street Presents: Follow That Bird. Half-Dressed Cartoon Animal: Wears a shirt and no pants. A Lizard Named "Liz": Is named "Hoots" and he's an owl.

characters.name: Kermit the Frog
characters.description: The Muppet Show'seasily-flustered host, here Kermit usually plays aroving news reporterin a trench coat. He also often attempts to give lectures to the audience which are inevitably ruined by another character.Jim Henson's definitive role; Kermit and Ernie aren't that different, acoustically speaking. This is especially apparent in Bert and Ernie'sMuppet Showguest appearance, where Ernie appears and speaks immediately after Kermit introduces the pair. See also his entry onCharacters.The Muppet Show. Affectionate Nickname: Cookie Monster, who Kermit tends to serve as afoilto, always addresses him as "Frog" or "Froggy". Grover calls him "Froggy" as well.Cookie Monster:No cookie, no guessing game with clues.Arrivederci, Frog. Beware the Nice Ones: Kermit is usually friendly and even-tempered, but when he's pushed too far he can get very angry indeed. Berserk Button: Played with on his part. On Sesame Street, in an early skit he and Joey sing the Alphabet, only for Joey to constantly refer to Cookie Monster as a letter in a playful manner, with Kermit getting more and more mock angry at her, before deciding to storm off. When Joey calls after him that she loves him, Kermit immediately returns to Joey, revealing it all to be a joke, and confirms he loves her too. Butt-Monkey: Frequently the victim of Grover's bumbling and Cookie Monster's hedonism, among other misfortunes.

characters.name: Little Bird
characters.description: He lives in a tree in front of 123 Sesame Street, and is a little friend of Big Bird's. In the 50th season premiere, he is revealed to be Big Bird's cousin. A Dog Named "Dog": A bird with "bird" in its last name.

characters.name: Mama and Papa Bear
characters.description: The parents of Baby Bear and Curly Bear. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: Papa Bear wears a hat and tie. Funny Animal: They're both anthro bears. Good Parents: They try to do what's best for both their cubs. Trademark Favorite Food: They like porridge as much as their son does.

characters.name: Preston Rabbit
characters.description: A postman rabbit who works at the Sesame Street Post Office. It Was a Gift: Well, he likes to deliver things to other characters. He once tried to give Elmo a sign that readsABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ. Elmo ended up singing the famous song originally sung by Big Bird. At that point, Big Bird and the kids told them that it's not a word, It's the alphabet.

characters.name: Shelly the Turtle
characters.description: A friendly but a slow-moving turtle. Shrinking Violet: He tends to be very shy, and it takes a bit of coaxing to help get him "out of his shell".

characters.name: Mr. Snuffleupagus
characters.description: A slow-talking, vaguely proboscidean creature and Big Bird's best friend. He originally wasn't thought to be real, but was revealed in a Season 17 episode. Abandoned Catchphrase: Snuffy used to always say "Oh, dear" in a worried voice. Big Bird even lampshaded it once; when Snuffy went missing in one episode and BB called the police (an Anything Muppet) to take a report, part of his description was that he said "Oh, dear" a lot. Characterization Marches On: He started out with a rather odd and perpetually sad personality as well as speaking with a rather creepy, echoing, sad voice. It wasn't until when Marty Robinson took over the character that, though still sad occasionally, his personality became more cheerful and his voice had a wider range of emotions. Early-Installment Weirdness: Snuffy used to have wide yellow eyes with green sclera and was understandably changed to a different lazy eyed design as the debut appearance was... unsettling, to say the least. The Eeyore: Used to be one of his defining character traits, but he steadily grew out of itas time went on.

characters.name: Barkley
characters.description: This large, playful Muppet dog is Linda's pet, who understands American Sign Language. When he debuted in Season 9, he was known as Woof Woof. In Season 10, he became Barkley after one episode dealt with changing his name by popular vote. By the start of the new millennium, Barkley hasn't appeared as often, but has been seen a couple times in recent years. Big Friendly Dog: A big, playful dog. Dog Walks You: When he runs while somebody is walking him, that somebody often gets pulled along. Hidden Eyes: His eyes are covered by his hair. Sick Episode: Catches a cold in one episode. It goes away, but thenhe turns invisible.

characters.name: Buster the Horse
characters.description: Forgetful Jones' trusty steed. Sapient Steed: Has a much better memory than his rider, and proves very helpful in reminding Jones to do things.

characters.name: Fluffy
characters.description: Oscar's pet elephant. The Faceless: All that is seen of her is her trunk sticking out of Oscar's can. Ironic Name: Elephants don't have much hair and are anything but fluffy. NO INDOOR VOICE: Sort of. Fluffy is known to trumpet quite loudly.

characters.name: Little Murray Sparkles
characters.description: Meaningful Name: The "Little" in his name comes from his small size.

characters.name: Ovejita
characters.description: Murray's lamb sidekick, who speaks only in Spanish. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: Wears a bow in her wool. Amazing Technicolor Wildlife: Is a purple sheep. A Dog Named "Dog": 'Ovejita' is Spanish for 'lamb'. Talking Animal: Is pretty much a normal lamb, but she speaks Spanish.

characters.name: Preposterous
characters.description: Dogs Are Dumb: And lazy. He doesn't do much of anything except chew on a rubber pickle. Sometimes he'll attack Oscar for no apparent reason.

characters.name: Ralphie
characters.description: Baby Bear's talented parrot. The Ace: Can play fetch, identify shapes, speak English, Spanish and Hamster, and even make fruit salad. Polly Wants a Microphone: He once said a whole sentence in Spanish, complementing Maria's blouse. Speaks Fluent Animal: Apparently, he speaks fluent Hamster.

characters.name: Slimey
characters.description: Filthy Fun: Likes to play in mud due to being a worm. Hidden Depths: Is a cute little talking worm, who's also been to space. Interspecies Romance: One episode inThe '80sgave him a caterpillar girlfriend named Scuzzina. Oscar is worried about how that would even work out. Morality Pet: A literal case; he's one of very few Sesame Street residents Oscar is usually not grouchy to. Space Episode: His trip to the moon took up several episodes.

characters.name: Sloppy
characters.description: Slimey's baby sister. Meaningful Name: Was named because she was born in the Sloppy Jalopy.

characters.name: Wolfgang the Seal
characters.description: Uncle Wally's pet seal. He debuted on season 20 (1988-1989) and continued to appear after his handler left the show in Season 23 (1991-1992). Animal Talk: He can only bark. Berserk Button: Not of the rage-inducing kind, but whatever you do, do NOT say "fish" aloud in his earshot. Trademark Favorite Food: Loves to eat fish. So much so, in fact, that if he so much as hears theword"fish", he goes into a barking frenzy.

characters.name: Worm astronauts
characters.description: A group of worms from around the world who travel to the moon and back in a spaceship called theWiggleprisein Season 29. Alphabetical Theme Naming: Most of them have names that start with S. Color-Coded Characters: Slimey is orange, Spaghettini is red, Squishta is pink, Legusano is purple, and Squashimi is blue. Multinational Team: The crew consists of Slimey from the United States, Spaghettini from Italy, Squishta from Romania, Legusano from Colombia, and Squashimi from Japan. Odd Name Out: Legusano is the only one whose name doesn't start with S.

characters.name: Colambo
characters.description: A black-fleeced sheep detective who solves the crime of the Fairy Tale / Mother Goose stories. Day in the Limelight: His last appearance — and arguably his finest hour — was in Episode 3902, where he helped Gabi search for Fluffy the elephant. No Celebrities Were Harmed: He is based onLieutenant Columbo.

characters.name: Flo Bear
characters.description: She is a bear writer. No Celebrities Were Harmed: She is based on the French writerGustave Flaubert.

characters.name: Jackman Wolf
characters.description: The VJ wolf who hostsThe Sesame Street Rock and Roll Request Show. No Celebrities Were Harmed: He is based the late radio announcer Wolfman Jack.

characters.name: Meryl Sheep
characters.description: A sheep who also happens to be an accomplished actress, she heads the Meryl Sheep School of Acting, and countsSusan Sarandonamong her students. Distaff Counterpart: Created as a female equivalent to Placido Flamingo, likewise being an animal parodying a famous performer. Furry Female Mane: She has a rather human-like head of hair (variously blonde and brown) along with her wool coat. No Celebrities Were Harmed: Obviously based onMeryl Streep. Non-Specifically Foreign: She has a vaguely Eastern European accent, inspired byMeryl Streep's role inSophie's Choice.

characters.name: The Oinker Sisters
characters.description: A trio of singing pigs, whose greatest hit is "A New Way to Walk". A Lizard Named "Liz": Their last name is "Oinker", which is because they are pigs and pigs say "oink". Fantastic Racism: In theDance Along!video, it's revealed they get offended by anyone saying "chops". No Celebrities Were Harmed: Their name is a riff on the Pointer Sisters. Special Person, Normal Name: One of the Oinker Sisters is named "Suie Oinker".

characters.name: Placido Flamingo
characters.description: An opera-singing flamingo. He is introduced by Phil Harmonic. Proud of his talents and not averse to the sound of his own voice, he helped in the introduction of classical music to the series. He is cited, along with the 1957Looney TunescartoonWhat's Opera, Doc?, as an effective and influential early introduction to the world of opera. No Celebrities Were Harmed: He is based onPlacido Domingo. Put on a Bus: He was dropped after Richard Hunt's death in 1992, but continued to appear in recycled segments until 1998. He made a cameo in a 2009 episode, on the front cover of a book bearing Hunt's name.

characters.name: The Squirelles
characters.description: A trio of singing squirrels who sing various doo-wop songs. No Celebrities Were Harmed: They are based on The Shirelles. Talking Animal: Are mostly normal squirrels but they can talk.

characters.name: Abby Cadabby
characters.description: A fairy who moved to Sesame Street during season 37. She's a 3-year-old fairy in training, who begins attending the Flying Fairy School in Season 40. All-Loving Hero: Abby sees the best in Oscar, and genuinely doesn't believe that he's that grouchy. That's gotta count forsomething. All Myths Are True: Abby's mom, Maggie Cadabby, is Cinderella's fairy godmother. The Apprentice: Hence"Abby's FlyingFairy School". Breakout Character: While only appearing in three episodes of Season 37, she became more prominent as the show went on and proved to be a great addition to the cast. She later gained her own solo segments, appears alongside Elmo in nearly all his guest appearances, and even got her own television special.

characters.name: Honkers & Dingers
characters.description: Two species of Muppet, one with a bicycle horn for a nose and the other with a table bell on top of its head, which they use instead of speaking. Alliterative Name: Most of them are unnamed, but Honkers sometimes have first names that start with H. The pink baby Honker is named Henrietta Honker, and in one episode, a family of Honkers who all have H names appear. Amazing Technicolor Population: Like monsters and AM's, they come in many different colors. Gag Nose: Honkers squeeze theirs in order to honk. Pink Means Feminine: The pink baby Henrietta Honker and her fuchsia mother Mrs. Honker are the Honker puppets most often depicted as female, and the baby Dinger has a pink nose and pink hair. However, the mother Dinger is green.

characters.name: Isabelle
characters.description: A small creature from the Furchester Hotel. Punny Name: She got the name because she "is a bell".

characters.name: Maggie Cadabby
characters.description: The mother of Abby, wife of Freddy, ex-wife of Mr. Cadabby, and stepmother of Rudy. She is a Fairy Godmother. Good Parents: She's always there when Abby needs advice. Interspecies Romance: She married a monster. Noodle Incident: Enforced. In order to make the message about divorce apply to as many people as possible, it's left ambiguous as to why she divorced Mr. Cadabby, besides "grown-up problems" that they "couldn't fix". Unseen No More: After nearly 10 years of merely beingThe Ghostwhom Abby would constant mention in conversations as theFairy Godmotherand call for help, she makes her first onscreen appearance in 2018, featured in several videos alongside her new husband Freddy produced forSesame Street in Communities. She made her first onscreen appearance on the show proper, in Episode 5026 in Season 50.

characters.name: Martians/Yip-Yips
characters.description: Jellyfish-like, hovering aliens with antennae, severe underbite, and a distinctive "yip yip yip yip uh-huh uh-huh" sound. An Alien Named "Bob": The primary two are named "Joe" and "Bob". Although in the game show sketchBring that Thing, Guy Smiley addressed them as "Stevie" and "Jonathan" Martians. Amusing Alien: Often seen doing funny things trying to figure out how Earth things work. Animal Sweet on Object: In their first encounter with a computer, the pink martian ends up falling in love with it, as it places aroseon its keyboard, followed by stroking the keyboard. Fish Out of Water: In their first few years, they were very unfamiliar with Earth, to the point where they spent most of their time attempting to communicate with inanimate objects.

characters.name: S.A.M. the Robot
characters.description: One of the early characters on the show, S.A.M. frequently claimed he was perfect, despite abundant evidence to the contrary. Adhesive Bow Tie: He wears a red bow tie decked out with white polka dots, which looks as if it's stuck to his chest. Given that he's a robot, it's possible it's held onto his metallic exterior by a magnet. Broken Record: S.A.M. will tell anyone who is around him that machines are perfect... except he'd always get stuck, so he'd say, "Machines are perfect — are perfect — are perfect..." until someone would get him unstuck by hitting him. Crying Wolf: In Episode 678, S.A.M. spends the day imitating various sounds, such as a windstorm, thunder, a fire engine, breaking glass, a marching band, an electric drill, and a whistling tea kettle. He ends with his imitation of an airplane, which Susan, Luis, and David mistake for Alphabet Bates' airplane until they find out the truth from Big Bird. When Alphabet Bates really does show up in his airplane, the adults think S.A.M. is still making imitations, even when Big Bird tries to tell them that Alphabet Bates' plane really has shown up. Do-Anything Robot: Efficiently, on the other hand.....

characters.name: Miscellaneous Muppets
characters.description: Let's Meet the Meat: Singing Food will cheerfully discuss how nutritious it is.

characters.name: The Baker
characters.description: Character who appears in the final segment of a series of counting shorts, unofficially named by fans as the "Baker Films". The Baker is a hapless individual who, after proclaiming (to trumpet fanfare) that he has a number of baked goods in his arms, attempts to walk down a short flight of steps, but ultimately he trips and spills everything, making a huge mess. Butt-Monkey: Pretty hard to view him as anything but this. No Name Given: He is never named. He just known to fans as the Baker.

characters.name: Bob Johnson
characters.description: An unassuming, low-key music teacher who lives in the apartment above Hooper's Store. Aerith and Bob: The literal "Bob" to his brother Minneapolis's Aerith. Aside Glance: Trying to teach the Two-Headed Monster to play the clarinet evokes a flustered look at the camera. Big Damn Heroes: Bob makes his sole appearance in the 38th season so thathe can coax Horatio the Elephant out of Maria's bathtub. Character Aged with the Actor: Arguably more visible than the others.

characters.name: David Hobson
characters.description: A young man who debuted in Season 2. Originally a law student who worked part time at Hooper's Store, he took over the store after Mr. Hooper's death in 1983. Cool Teacher: In a sketch where he plays a professor doing a lecture on trees. Cool Uncle: To his niece Akim, who appeared a few times in Seasons 13-15 as a teen, often assisting him at the store. David once mentioned a brother named Gregory, who is probably Akim's father. Put on a Bus: Moved away from Sesame Street to look after his elderly grandmother after Season 20 and sold the store to Mr. Handford. Raised by Grandparents: It's implied that he was this growing up, since his grandmother is the closest thing to a parent of his to appear on the show.

characters.name: Gordon Robinson
characters.description: A father figure to theMuppetsand kids on the street, and thede factoleader when things go wrong. Bald of Authority: From the beginning he was the street'sTeam Dad, but once Roscoe Orman took over the role he specifically became this type. The Bus Came Back: Gordon returned in a Season 54 and a Season 55 episode taking a much prominent role there. It is also revealed he retired from teaching and Nina was one of his students. Character Aged with the Actor: Just like the other humans. Cool Teacher: He's a middle school science teacher.

characters.name: Grace Hobson
characters.description: Country Mouse: She lives on a farm and once argued with David over whether country life was better than city life. Parental Substitute: Is hinted to have raised David, since his parents are never seen. Sassy Black Woman: She can be rather outspoken at times.

characters.name: Mr. Hooper
characters.description: A grandfather figure to those around him, and the original owner of Hooper's Store. Accidental Misnaming: That'sHooper, Big Bird,Hooper! Alliterative Name: His full name isHaroldHooper. Ambiguously Jewish: At least until Bob wished him a Happy Hanukkah inChristmas Eve on Sesame Street. Blind Without 'Em: In one episode during the era when everyone thought Snuffy was imaginary, he came face-to-face with Snuffy, but couldn't see him because he had lost his glasses.

characters.name: Linda
characters.description: A librarian and Bob's (apparent) girlfriend. Also deaf. Initially, she wasBarkley's owner, before he became the community's pet upon her departure. The Bus Came Back: In Sesame Street’s 50th Anniversary Celebration. Character Aged with the Actor: Shows her age in the 50th anniversary special. Disabled Snarker: She once subbed forOscar. That's got to count for something. Inspirationally Disadvantaged: Averted at actress Linda Bove's request. Both the actress and the character are deaf, but Bove specifically requested that her deafness not be treated as the defining aspect of the character, and that the writers not shy away from jokes about ASL.

characters.name: Luis Rodriguez
characters.description: A Chicano who runs the Fix-It Shop with Maria. Character Aged with the Actor: In later years, Luis along with the rest of the adults starts to show his old age. The Character Died with Him: Heavily implied by Elmo on social media. Gratuitous Spanish: Not so much these days, now that Rosita's around. Happily Married: Married to Maria.

characters.name: Mr. Macintosh
characters.description: A fruit vendor at the arch next to Hooper's Store. Meaningful Name: A fruit peddler who shares the name Macintosh with a type of apple, which is part of Apple's logo.

characters.name: Maria Rodriguez (née Figueroa)
characters.description: Maria came to Sesame Street from Puerto Rico. She worked as Luis' employee (and eventual co-partner) before settling down, marrying him, and having a daughter, Gabriela. Aborted Arc:She was hooked up with David until the mid-1980s.According to Louise Gikow, who wrote for various international co-productions, the reason why the David–Maria romance angle was dropped was due to health problems involving David's actor, Northern Calloway. Calloway had been battling mental illness since the 17th season began in 1985, and by the time the 20th season ended in 1989, he became so ill and ill-looking that he had to leave the show, dying of excited delirium complications only a year later in 1990. She was hooked up with David until the mid-1980s. According to Louise Gikow, who wrote for various international co-productions, the reason why the David–Maria romance angle was dropped was due to health problems involving David's actor, Northern Calloway. Calloway had been battling mental illness since the 17th season began in 1985, and by the time the 20th season ended in 1989, he became so ill and ill-looking that he had to leave the show, dying of excited delirium complications only a year later in 1990. All Women Love Shoes: At one point, she goes shoe-shopping and ends up trying on eighty pairs before finally finding the right ones for her.

characters.name: The Number Painter
characters.description: A smocked painter who paints a given number from 2 to 11 anywhere, including public and private property. His character appeared in a series of 10 segments teaching number shape recognition and how the number is drawn. These would air throughout the 1970s and 1980s; Benedict's co-stars in these shorts were Stockard Channing and Jerome Raphael. Chase Scene: One short, in which he painted an 8 on the bald head of a man in a pool, ended with anundercrankscene of the bald guy chasing the Painter around the pool. Inner Monologue: All of his lines. Mad Libs Catchphrase: "(I'm) going to paint a[numeral]". No Name Given: Like the Baker, he never gets a name.

characters.name: Olivia Robinson
characters.description: Gordon's sister and a professional photographer. Deadpan Snarker: She was not above taking good-natured jabs at her neighbors.[sees Big Bird's picture of David]A little young, don't you think? Sassy Black Woman: A bit more outspoken than Susan.

characters.name: Susan Robinson
characters.description: Gordon's wife and, as such, a maternal figure to those around her. Character Aged with the Actor. In the 2000s you can start to see Susan’s age, along with the rest of the humans. Happily Married: To Gordon. Parents Walk In at the Worst Time: Including one incident where Miles didn't want her to see the chaos happening in his room. Team Mom: To everyone on the street.

characters.name: Gabi Rodriguez
characters.description: Maria and Luis' daughter and a close friend to Gordon and Susan's son Miles. Birthday Episode: She has her eighth birthday in one episode. Character Aged with the Actor: Her second actress literally grew up onSesame Street, and the character later took on aCool Big Sisrole to the Muppets. Real-Life Relative: The first Gabi, Gabriela Rose Reagan, is Sonia Manzano's real-life daughter. In fact the character was created to workManzano's pregnancyinto the show. But the part was eventuallyrecastwhen Manzano realized that little Gabriela didn't enjoy acting. Sick Episode: In one episode, she has a mild flu on her birthday.

characters.name: Gina Jefferson
characters.description: She started out as an assistant at Hooper's Store duringThe '80s. A lot has changed since then, and now she's a veterinarian. Character Development: In the span of 24 years, she has assisted at Hooper's Store and a daycare, gone to veterinary school, opened a veterinary practice, and adopted her own son, Marco. Character Aged with the Actor: Grows up, becomes a vet, and adopts a son. Cool Big Sis: Originally started out as this during her teenage years. Genki Girl: Occasionally showed shades of this during her teenage years.

characters.name: Hiroshi
characters.description: A Japanese-American artist and vet on Sesame Street. Gratuitous Japanese: He taught some of the residents a few Japanese words and phrases, such as "Domo arigato" ("Thank you very much.")

characters.name: Miles Robinson
characters.description: In the mid-80s, Susan and Gordon adopted a son. Miles went from being a younger sibling type character to being an older brother figure to the Muppet characters. Miles had a close friendship with Maria and Luis' daughter, Gabi.

characters.name: Uncle Wally
characters.description: Bob's humorous and warm-hearted uncle who loves to tell tall tales. Cool Old Guy: Uncle Wally seemed to take over this role after Mr. Hooper's death. Manchild: His constant telling of tall tales and precocious personality made him one.

characters.name: Angela
characters.description: Happily Married: She is married to Jamal, and has a baby daughter named Kayla.

characters.name: Carlo
characters.description: A teenager who was a student in Gordon's science class. In 1995, he started working at Hooper's Store.

characters.name: Celina
characters.description: A very empathetic dance instructor who taught many different forms of dance.

characters.name: Mr. Handford
characters.description: A retired firefighter and the owner of Hooper's Store between David and Alan. Accidental Misnaming: Snuffy would sometimes call him "Mr. Handfoot". Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Unlike his predecessors, we never find out what happened to him (or his assistant Carlo, for that matter, who vanished at the same time that he did). Sesame Workshop's official website states that he sold the store to Alan, but that still doesn't explain why neither he nor Carlo are seen on Sesame Street anymore, or where they went after he sold the store. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: When Leonard Jackson played him. Nice Guy: When Dave Smyrl took over.

characters.name: Jamal
characters.description: A park ranger of the Sesame Street park. Happily Married: He is married to Angela and has a baby daughter named Kayla.

characters.name: Lillian Edwards
characters.description: Friend to All Children: She runs a daycare out of her own home and gets along very well with the kids she looks after. Large Ham: Compared to most of the human cast, she can be pretty over-the-top in her performance, especially when she's singing.

characters.name: Ruthie
characters.description: Owner of the Finders Keepers thrift store. Commuting on a Bus: Ruthie was prominent from 1993 to 1998 when she was owner of Finders Keepers, but when the Around The Corner set was removed after the 29th season, she continued to appear but only in segments than on the street.

characters.name: Savion
characters.description: A young male friend of Gina's and a famous dancer.

characters.name: Alan
characters.description: Call-Back: He debuted in the first episode to featureElmo's World, when he hosted a huge Birdketeer meeting, and was in over his head. In the first episode to featureElmo the Musical, he knows what he's dealing with, and tries to nip chaos in the bud during another big event. Fat and Skinny: He is skinny and friends with fellow and only co-worker Chris Robinson, who is chubbier. Hilarity Ensues: He tends to get dragged into Muppet hijinks. Iconic Item: A dish towel, frequently on his shoulder. Nice Guy: After Bob, he's probably the biggest sweetheart in the human cast (although some might say that he's a little more high-strung).

characters.name: Armando
characters.description: An energetic young Puerto Rican writer. Always interested in trying new things and encouraging his Muppet friends to be true to themselves. Mando also loves technology. In-Series Nickname: Sometimes goes by Mando. Remember the New Guy?: Like most of the show's characters, Mando didn't get aWelcome Episode. He was just a character that everyone on the street already knew.

characters.name: Charlie
characters.description: A young girl with military parents who moves to Sesame Street. All-Loving Hero: She likes making friends with everyone on Sesame Street, even trying to befriend Oscar. Cheerful Child: She's very cheerful and happy. Military Brat: Her parents were in the military before moving to Sesame Street.

characters.name: Chris Robinson
characters.description: Gordon's nephew who came to Sesame Street looking for a job, and took one at Hooper's Store, to pay for college. Big Fun: He’s overweight, very cheerful, and also sometimes takes Elmo and his friends to somewhere fun such as taking Elmo camping in one episode. Butt-Monkey: Sometimes, this is because Alan is facing similar circumstances, and he needs Chris's help. Fat and Skinny: He is chubby and friends with Alan who is a lot thinner. Manchild: Often very enthusiastic about things like circuses or bubbles and such.

characters.name: Nina
characters.description: A bilingual Hispanic college student who now owns the bicycle shop (formerly owned by Luis) and also works at the laundromat (formerly operated by Leela). Cool Big Sis: She acts very compassionate towards the younger Muppet characters, with a hint of herTeam Mompersonality.

characters.name: Mr. Noodle and family
characters.description: An oddly dressedvaudevillianmime who lives outside the window of Elmo's World. The role is occasionally performed by Mr. Noodle's brother Mr. Noodle, his sister Miss Noodle, or his other sister Miss Noodle. Big Friendly Dog: Mr. Noodle, the brother, owns one namedSchmoodle. That he takes a couple of tries to play fetch with successfully. The Ditz: The Noodles' role is to provide a character to whom 3-year-old viewers can feel superior. Literal-Minded: Another part of the fact that they seldom do anything right and are always getting it wrong as per theirComically Missing the Pointroutine is one of these from time to time. One-Steve Limit: Averted. Of course, all the Noodles are pretty much interchangeable.

characters.name: Sofia
characters.description: A Latina character who appears in resource videos, her first beingLittle Children, Big Challenges: Incarceration. Prison Episode: Sofia told Alex that when she was Alex's age, her father was also incarcerated, She taught everybody that incarcerated means that when somebody violates the law (an adult rule), they have to go to jail or prison.

characters.name: Charlie the Chef
characters.description: He Who Must Not Be Seen: He is only mentioned by Grover. Suddenly Voiced: Charlie was usually a silent character. But in the Russian restaurant skit, he replied to Grover, "NYET!" That means "NO!" in Russian. He says it when they are out of those certain foods.

characters.name: Mr. Cadabby
characters.description: Noodle Incident: Enforced. To keep the message applicable, it's unclear why he and Maggie got a divorce beyond irreparable "grown-up problems". Unnamed Parent: While his surname is "Cadabby", his first name is unrevealed.

characters.name: Mrs. Johnson
characters.description: The wife of Grover the Waiter's costumer: Mr. Johnson. She Who Must Not Be Seen: She has been never seen in puppet form, though in one segment, Mr. Johnson brought in a painting of his wife to the frame shop to put in a picture frame. Vague Age: She looks elderly, but her husband is middle-aged.

characters.name: Spencer
characters.description: Suspiciously Similar Substitute: Ruthie fills in for Spencer onThe Number 4 Dance.

characters.name: Blogg
characters.description: Cloud Cuckoo Lander: Likes gross things like earwax and belly button lint and does other pretty dang wacky things. Deep Sleep: He once fell under an enchanted sleep fromeating a poisoned apple. Half-Breed Angst: Blogg is half-troll and half-fairy, so he lives in a troll town but goes to a fairy school. He doesn't mind being half-troll at the fairy school, but when his classmates and teacher visit his hometown with him, he denies that he's half-fairy to the citizens and hides his wings. Two Guys and a Girl: He and Gonnigan serve as the Two Guys to Abby's Girl.

characters.name: Bobby
